thread:
jess_support: Customer reporting console graphs just spin and then show 'No data' across multiple dashboards. Happens for entire org workspace, started ~2024-11-19 09:12 UTC. Customer seeing 504s from analytics API when hitting /v2/query. sample from their side:
```
GET /v2/query?panel=heatmap HTTP/1.1
Host: analytics.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED

HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-correlation-id: c8f3b2d4-9a1e-4f8a-90f3-3287a1b2d111
```
jess_support: They said it was working before they rotated an org service-account key yesterday. No account-wide outages in status page. Escalating, attaching correlation id above.
matt_oncall: got it. I'll pull logs for c8f3b2d4-9a1e-4f8a-90f3-3287a1b2d111 from analytics cluster. Any repro steps the customer gave?
jess_support: They repro by opening the dashboard, selecting last 30m, and hitting refresh. Happens in both Chrome and Safari, incognito too. Said rolling back the key fixes other services but console still 504s.
matt_oncall: looking at analytics-api logs -> seeing repeated upstream timeouts to authz service: "POST /auth/validate 504 upstream timeout" for same correlation id. Short log snippet:
```
[2024-11-19T09:12:11Z] correlation=c8f3b2d4... lvl=warn msg="upstream request timeout" upstream=authz-service path=/auth/validate attempt=1
[2024-11-19T09:12:12Z] correlation=c8f3b2d4... lvl=error msg="failed to authorize request" status=504
```
viv_reliability: did we deploy any authz changes or cert rotations yesterday? I remember a key rotation for org-credentials job. Could be hitting a stale cache or a blocked service account.
sam_frontend: frontend gets a 504 upstream for the panel fetch call -> we show spinner then "No data". If analytics-api returns 401/403 we'd show auth error, but 504 suggests authz-service itself timing out. Is there a fallback route to the legacy authz cluster?
matt_oncall: pinging authz oncall. Meanwhile can customer share the exact service-account email they rotated? want to check mapping.
jess_support: they gave sa: dashboard-ingest@acme-corp. They say it was rotated with new key ID K-2024-11-18.
viv_reliability: checking authz logs for that service-account: looks like the token verifier pool can't reach kms endpoint intermittently after the rotation; I see errors: "kms: GetKeyMetadata timeout" and also spike in DNS failures to kms.internal.
matt_oncall: hmm could be egress firewall rule change or transient DNS; but customer said only they rotated a key, not network changes. Could rotation have triggered extra verification calls causing rate-limiting on KMS side?
sam_frontend: we can short-circuit verification for requests with org-scoped fallback if we detect failing KMS, but that's invasive. Short-term: does rolling back the key on their side make graphs return? They said rolling back fixed other services but console still 504. Maybe our cached mapping still points to the new key and KMS lookup for the new key is failing.
viv_reliability: I'll try forcing a cache refresh on authz service for the customer's org mapping. Doing: `POST /internal/refresh-org-cache?org=acme-corp`
[system action]
deploy-bot: POST /internal/refresh-org-cache?org=acme-corp -> 202 Accepted (task queued)
matt_oncall: cache refresh queued. Also increasing authz-service timeout to 8s for requests from analytics cluster while we investigate (temporary).
[system action]
deploy-bot: authz-service timeout config updated -> applied to cluster analytics-prod-1
matt_oncall: asking customer to retry now.
jess_support: customer retried at 09:15 UTC. They reported graphs loaded for a few panels, but large dashboards still have a couple 504s. correlation id for a failing panel: a3d9f7b0-4b2c-4b5f-a3c2-9f2d6b4a2222
matt_oncall: looking at logs for a3d9f7b0... now I see the authz call succeeded but the analytics worker timed out waiting on a KV cache fetch: "kv-cache: timeout fetching prefix shards". That aligns with heavy cache eviction after key rotation jobs.
viv_reliability: so two issues layered: KMS/DNS timeouts for key verification and then KV cache thundering causing some queries to exceed our SLO. Proposed plan:
- keep authz timeout bumped for 1 hour
- prime KV cache for the affected org (warm prefixes)
- ask customer to re-run dashboards and confirm
- follow-up postmortem to track KMS DNS flakiness and cache strategy
sam_frontend: I can add a UX tweak to show a clearer hint when panels fail due to upstream timeouts (include correlation id and retry button). Low risk.
matt_oncall: I primed the hot prefixes for acme-corp; also triggered a soft restart of a few analytics workers to rebalance cache.
[system action]
deploy-bot: restarted analytics-worker pool shards {12,13,14} -> success
jess_support: customer retried at 09:22 UTC and says dashboards are back to normal. They asked what caused it so they can avoid in future.
viv_reliability: short answer: their key rotation triggered additional KMS validation calls which hit intermittent DNS/egress hiccups; that caused authz timeouts and a subsequent cache eviction spike that led to 504s on heavy queries. We're capturing next steps in incident ticket INC-2024-789.
matt_oncall: marking as resolved for support. Will follow up with SLA-impact assessment and PM on UX message. :white_check_mark:
jess_support: thanks team. I emailed customer summary and link to INC-2024-789. Closing the support case after their confirmation. :thumbsup:
